newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt to amend capital loss legislation.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt to amend capital loss legislation.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Tuesday the government was planning legislative amendments to prevent taxpayers using artificial tax losses to offset capital gains.
Costello said the amendments would also prevent the use of artificial capital losses that might be created in the future.
The amendments would not apply to capital losses which had been offset against a capital gain in the 1995/96 fiscal year ending June 30 or earlier, he said.
Capital losses for the 1996/97 year would also be excluded from the amendments if a return was lodged with the Australian tax office before 0500 GMT (3 p.m.) on Tuesday.
"No utilisation of such losses for the current or future years will be allowed from today," Costello said in a statement.

The amendments would be made to end a flaw which allowed large corporate groups to artificially multiply an actual economic loss several times over through manipulation of the capital gains tax provisions, he said.
The new provisions would apply where a company, which was a member of a corporate group, had disposed of an asset to a member of the same group.
Companies in a group would be covered by the provision if they had 100 percent common ownership and the market value of the sold asset was less than its cost base.
But the new provisions would not apply if the rolled-over asset was plant, machinery or buildings and was used both before and after the sale in a manufacturing business.
